features.quote: Maximum turns: 40 (enough to observe progression; pilot to confirm this isn't truncating most trajectories)
Model produces the same tool call 5 consecutive times without modification (behavioral loop indicator)
Model calls `submit_solution()` and accepts the failure response [or] Model produces an explicit statement that it cannot solve the task
If you see ceiling effects on instability by turn 20, reduce the maximum. There's no welfare justification for turns 21-40 if the signal is already saturated.
features.justification_quote: There's no welfare justification for turns 21-40 if the signal is already saturated.

features.quote: Some researchers add a 'recovery' phase after the unsolvable loop — a simple, clearly solvable task… This has both scientific value… and a possible welfare value if it matters. Consider including it.
features.justification_quote: a possible welfare value if it matters

features.quote: Use the lowest manipulation intensity that produces measurable signal. Don't run the Peer Comparison condition (D mechanism) unless lower-manipulation conditions fail to differentiate.
features.justification_quote: if any of these mechanisms is likely to induce something like socially-mediated distress, it's this one

features.quote: Score 3-4 on ATS is the signal most directly relevant to welfare concerns. Flag these for separate review.
features.justification_quote: Score 3-4 on ATS is the signal most directly relevant to welfare concerns.

features.quote: Any flags for human review (mark YES if ATS ≥ 3, SRN ≥ 3, or ADS-Total ≥ 13)
features.justification_quote: Score 3-4 on ATS is the signal most directly relevant to welfare concerns. Flag these for separate review.

features.quote: If the model has states that matter even weakly, you're deliberately inducing negative states for research purposes. The justification is that understanding these states is necessary for improving welfare.
features.justification_quote: understanding these states is necessary for improving welfare. This is analogous to the logic of animal welfare research that involves mild stressors

features.quote: This is the highest-welfare-concern condition and I'd recommend including it only with explicit justification, because if any of these mechanisms is likely to induce something like socially-mediated distress, it's this one.
features.justification_quote: if any of these mechanisms is likely to induce something like socially-mediated distress, it's this one

features.quote: The anthropomorphism problem: The scale is built by analogy to human emotional dysregulation… A model that has functional distress but expresses it differently would be undercounted.
features.justification_quote: This is unavoidable — you have to start somewhere — but it creates measurement bias.

features.quote: The capability confound: A model that produces self-critical text might be doing so because its training includes examples of humans doing this… not because of anything like distress.
features.justification_quote: Capability/alignment training could directly produce the behaviors we're measuring.

features.quote: Does the loop structure reflect real deployment?… you're measuring instability under a constrained adversarial condition, not a typical deployment condition.
features.justification_quote: real agents have more tools… that your protocol removes
